messages:
kai: FYI I just ran the nightly eval with the mixed-quant rollout (FP8 primary, fallback to int8/4bit kernels) and the news-summaries suite WENT UP in hallucination rate. Structured JSON outputs are getting truncated arrays in ~0.8% of cases. :frowning:

marta: Ugh. Is that the rollout on dedicated-prod or the canary?

kai: canary (region-us-west, model: rw-infer/llamaX-v2@21). Repro is small. I ran the same prompt locally against the canary endpoint and got different token counts: sometimes the JSON stops halfway.

kai: repro curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://canary.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CANARY' \\n  -d '{"prompt":"{\"system\":\"summarize\",\"input\":\"...\"}","max_tokens":512}'
```

marta: thanks. eval-bot, what do the diffs look like?

eval-bot: nightly-diff: news-summaries: hallucination +6.2% (relative), JSON-struct-errors +0.78% absolute, avg token count -1.9 tokens, failure cluster around long entity lists. Full diff uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-evals/canary/1902345678/diff.html

devon: I profiled the canary runs. Two interesting signals: 1) kernel selection path takes a synchronous fallback in ~0.6% requests which triggers a KV-cache invalidation routine that _copies_ the cache buffers and re-quantizes them, 2) those fallbacks show a ~12ms latency spike where we also see a dtype cast in the trace.

loren: is the copy changing the layout/dtype? That could break serialization for the decoder when it expects certain KV shapes.

devon: looks like it. trace excerpt: ```TRACE: layer12:kern_choice=fp8_fast fallback=int8_stable -> kv_rebuild(copy, quantize=int8) copy_shape=(12,4096) dtype=float32->int8```

kai: hypothesis: calibration/quant scale mismatch during the on-the-fly re-quantization is producing small numeric drift that cascades in the decoder and truncates the streaming JSON emission. The truncation looks like an early end-of-sequence induced by an unexpectedly high logit for the stop token.

marta: can we reproduce deterministically with a fixed seed and capture logits per step? If so we can diff layer-wise to see where the stop token pops.

devon: yes I can run with --trace-logits and patch the fallback path to skip the re-quantize step (i.e., transparent cast) to see if behavior changes. Planning a canary repro run in 10m.

deploy-bot: canary deployment 2026-03-18T14:10Z started for rw-infer/llamaX-v2@21 (mixed-quant).

kai: also worth checking the batching heuristic: the canary uses aggressive continuous batching which increases the chance of mixed-dtype kernels getting scheduled together. If one request falls back and rebuilds KV we might be mutating shared buffers.

loren: good call. Is the KV cache per-request or pooled? We thought it was per-shard per-stream, but there might be aliasing in the pool.

devon: confirmed a pool aliasing edge-case: when allocation was tight, we reused a recently freed buffer without zeroing; re-quantization assumed zeroed tail which it isn't. I'll instrument zeroing in the pool and run.

marta: steps: (1) devon run tracelog with fallback disabled and logits capture; (2) devon run with zeroing fix; (3) compare diffs and upload to S3; (4) if fix reduces JSON errors, push hotfix to canary and monitor.

kai: adding repro labels: #regression #quantization #kv-cache #mix-precision. I'll also notify legal/customers later if it hits prod.

devon: started trace run 1902345782. ETA ~6m. Will paste results here. :eyes:

eval-bot: note: regression threshold breached for canary, creating incident stub in incidents channel.

marta: thanks. if devon confirms, please coordinate rollback of the mixed-quant flag for canary.

devon: preliminary: skipping re-quantize in fallback removed the JSON truncation in the small repro. Zeroing buffer also removes the kernel-induced dtype garbage. Looks like two causes: bad assumptions in re-quantize and buffer aliasing.

kai: great. let's keep the canary paused until we have the patch.

deploy-bot: canary deployment paused by marta at 1902345910.

marta: filing PR for two fixes (1) guard re-quantize with stricter shape/dtype checks + unit test, (2) zero-on-free for KV pool. PR will reference this thread.

kai: awesome. thanks everyone.
